title: Install-time credential exfiltration
description: A lifecycle script (preinstall/postinstall) collects environment variables or token files such as ~/.npmrc, encodes them, and sends them to a remote host. Benign explanation to rule out: telemetry or build tooling that only sends non-secret metadata and documents it.

title: Dependency hijack with targeted payload
description: A previously trusted package gains a new dependency or file containing an encrypted/encoded payload that is decoded and evaluated only under specific conditions. Public example: event-stream 3.3.6 added flatmap-stream (2018).

title: Account takeover release with downloader
description: A hijacked maintainer account publishes versions whose install script downloads and runs a binary (e.g. a cryptominer). Public example: ua-parser-js 0.7.29, 0.8.0, 1.0.0 (2021).

title: System reconnaissance beacon
description: Install-time code collects hostname, username and network interfaces and sends them via HTTP or DNS lookups. Seen in dependency-confusion probes. Benign explanation to rule out: security-research canaries that disclose themselves.

title: Obfuscated dynamic code
description: Large high-entropy strings decoded and passed to eval/new Function hide the real behaviour from reviewers. Benign explanation to rule out: legitimate minified bundles or WebAssembly loaders, which usually come from a documented build step.
